kind.text: I am steady. I do not need to be finished to be worthy of rest. When something is hard, I can slow down, ask for help, and speak to myself as I would to a friend.
You can be patient with yourself the way you are patient with a friend who is learning. You are allowed to go slowly. You are allowed to begin again, and the beginning still counts.
Wherever there is a human being, there is an opportunity for a kindness.
kind.author: Seneca

kind.text: I do not have to earn rest by finishing everything first. Rest is part of the work, not a reward for it. I can stop when I am tired and start again when I am ready.
My worth is not measured by how much I get done today. A slow day is still a day I lived well. I will do what I can and let that be enough.
The way I talk to myself matters. Today I will use the tone I would use with someone I care about. If I would not say it to a friend, I do not need to say it to myself.
Making a mistake means I tried something. I can name what went wrong without deciding what it says about me. Then I fix what I can and move on to the next thing.
Patience with others begins with patience for myself. When I am gentle with my own slow progress, I have more gentleness left over for everyone else.
Everyone I meet today is carrying something I cannot see. I do not need to know what it is to be kind. A little warmth costs me nothing and may be the best part of someone's day.
Being tired is a signal, not a verdict on my effort. When I am worn out, the kind response is rest, not a lecture. I can give myself what I would gladly give anyone else.
Not every thought about myself is true. The thought that I am not enough is a thought, not a fact. I can notice it, name it, and go back to what I was doing.
I am allowed to go slowly. Starting again is not failing; it is how anything gets learned. Each new beginning counts as much as the first one did.
What you do makes a difference, and you have to decide what kind of difference you want to make.
kind.author: Jane Goodall
kind.work: Reason for Hope and public talks

kind.text: I can treat myself with patience without avoiding responsibility. I can acknowledge a mistake, correct what I can, and continue.
I can be honest without being harsh. Clear words and a calm tone can exist together.
I do not need perfect words to show care. Listening carefully and responding with respect are often enough.
Kindness does not require agreement. I can respect another person while holding my own view.
I can be present for myself before trying to fix anything. Paying attention to what hurts is already a form of care.
When I am hurt, I can ask for help instead of expecting others to guess what I need. Honest words can make repair possible.
Understanding takes attention, time, and a willingness to listen. I can offer those before deciding what another person means.

pres.text: Right now there is a breath moving in and out. I can feel my feet on the floor and the weight of my hands. Nothing in this moment needs solving. I only need to be here for it.
I do not have to feel calm to act well. I can be unsettled and still do the next small thing. Steadiness usually follows action, not the other way around.
When everything feels like too much, I am usually carrying the whole day at once. I can set the day down. The next ten minutes are all I have to manage, and I can manage ten minutes.
I can only do one thing at a time. When my mind runs ahead to the next task, I bring it back to the one in my hands. This one is the only one I can actually do.
Worry about the future does not change the future. It only spends the present. I will bring my attention back to what is in front of me and do that one thing well.
A hard moment is one moment. It does not have to become the whole day. I can let it be what it is and notice when it passes.
Listening is about being present, not just about being quiet.
pres.author: Krista Tippett

pres.text: How we spend our days is, of course, how we spend our lives.
pres.author: Annie Dillard

pres.text: The present moment is filled with joy and happiness. If you are attentive, you will see it.
pres.author: Thich Nhat Hanh

pres.text: I can do one thing at a time. When my attention wanders, I can bring it back without judging myself.
I do not need to solve everything at once. I can give my full attention to what is in front of me.
This moment does not need to be remarkable to matter. I can notice it clearly and take part in it.
My mind may return to the past or move ahead to the future. I can notice that and come back to what I am doing.
Slowing down does not mean falling behind. It helps me see what deserves my attention.
I do not need to rush toward the next moment. I can stop, breathe, and give my attention to what is happening now.
Rest begins when I stop treating this moment as only a step toward the next one. I can let myself be here without needing to get somewhere else.
A strong feeling can be present without taking over. I can notice it, breathe, and wait before deciding what to do.
My destination is the here and now, the only time and place where true life is possible.
pres.author: Thich Nhat Hanh

persp.text: Most of what worries me today will not matter in a year. I can hold my plans loosely and let the day change them. What is mine to do, I will do. What is not mine, I can set down.
I do not have to force today into the shape I planned. When something will not bend, I can bend instead. I will do the task in front of me, stop when it is done, and let that be enough.
Some things are in our control and others not. Things in our control are opinion, pursuit, desire, aversion, and, in a word, whatever are our own actions.
persp.author: Epictetus

persp.text: Some things are up to me: my effort, my attention, my words. Most other things are not. I will put my energy where it can make a difference and let the rest go.
Don't demand that things happen as you wish, but wish that they happen as they do happen, and you will go on well.
persp.author: Epictetus

persp.text: I cannot control the outcome, only the attempt. I will make the attempt as well as I can and then let the result be what it is. That is the whole of my job.
A hard day is still only one day. Tomorrow starts fresh whether today went well or not. I will finish what I can, sleep, and begin again.
Most of the things we say or do are not necessary; get rid of them, and you will gain time and tranquillity.
persp.author: Marcus Aurelius

persp.text: Discomfort is the price of admission to a meaningful life.
persp.author: Susan David
persp.work: The Gift and Power of Emotional Courage, TED (2017)

persp.text: Real change, enduring change, happens one step at a time.
persp.author: Ruth Bader Ginsburg

persp.text: Not everything that is faced can be changed, but nothing can be changed until it is faced.
persp.author: James Baldwin
persp.work: As Much Truth as One Can Bear (1962)

persp.text: A difficult moment is not the whole story. I can respond to what is happening now and let the next step come afterward.
Progress does not need to be fast to be real. I can continue at a pace I can sustain.
Changing my mind when I learn something new is a strength. I do not have to defend an outdated view.
I can take useful criticism without accepting every judgment. I will keep what helps and leave the rest.
I can pause before trusting my first interpretation. There may be more to this situation than I can see right now.
I can release an expectation that is making life harder. Letting go of one fixed idea may make room for a better way forward.
The future is shaped by how I meet this moment. I can take care of what is here instead of carrying everything that may come next.
